script.base: Market prices a tight game: PHI implied 24.0, KC 22.5, no blowout. PHI wants Barkley (18 carries, 60 yards) and Hurts (11/65) on the ground, but KC blitzed 39% and Hurts was -0.46 EPA/db vs blitz (+0.41 when not blitzed), with tackle Cameron Williams out and target leader Dallas Goedert out, so PHI dropbacks should be messy and short. KC's Week 1 pass game already sat on Marquise Brown (16 targets, 99 yards, 101 air) with Xavier Worthy doubtful and Jalen Royals out; PHI blitzed only 18% and Mahomes was fine either way (0.31 EPA/db vs blitz, 0.24 vs none), but a 22.5 team total and a soft PHI run defense (5.41 YPC) do not require another 16-target day.
script.flip1: KC's blitz and the missing PHI tackle turn Hurts into a scrambler (he already had 11 rushes for 65). PHI falls behind, Barkley's rush share dies, deep shots to Dotson (3 targets, 48 air, 59 yards) stall, and the total slides under 46.5 while KC can run late.
script.flip2: PHI controls the ground, leads, and clocks it. Barkley carries rise, PHI WR routes dry up after the first half, and KC chases so Brown/JuJu/Thornton/Kelce targets spike in a pass-heavy comeback or a mild shootout above 46.5.

T Cameron Williams Out (shoulder) raises pressure and cuts rush efficiency and deep WR yards; PHI already failed vs the blitz. QB Tanner McKee Questionable (thumb) does not change Hurts's props. KC WR Xavier Worthy Doubtful (shoulder) had only 1 carry/0 yards and no listed targets in Week 1, so a sit adds little versus that box score but removes a Week 2 deep option; Jalen Royals Out (knee) has no Week 1 line in the pack. If Worthy sits, leftover looks go to Marquise Brown, JuJu Smith-Schuster (5/55/29), Tyquan Thornton (4/41/115 air) and Travis Kelce (4/47/24). Sources: pack injury report and Week 1 target/carry lines.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. KC took Brown away again and the blitz plus Williams being out made Hurts run, as he did for 65 yards on 11 carries, so Goedert's 7 targets never became Brown looks and he finished under 8.5 on one empty screen. Barkley missed 24.5 because the checkdowns were the same behind-the-line throws as Week 1 (-5 air, 4.8 yards per target): six targets still made about 20 yards, or Hurts scrambled on third down and Barkley stayed at five targets. One game made both rungs look like edges, and there was no sharp price to show the stand-in was wrong.
slip_story: One modest PHI script, not a shootout and not a KC chase: Goedert out and a 39% blitz feed Barkley underneath while Brown's WR1 floor clears 8.5 without needing explosives. Those two can win together in a 24-22 game. Do not add Dotson over 59.5, Hollywood over 99.5, or a total over; those need the clean-pocket or KC-chase flip. No TD legs. One market per player. Price edge unproven, so this is a candidate read only.
